title: Planning a Campus Recycling Project
context: A tutor and three students discuss how to organise a student project promoting recycling on campus.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Right, thanks for coming in. So today we need to plan the recycling awareness project for the student union. Who wants to start?

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: I can start. I think the main aim should be getting more students to use the recycling bins properly, because at the moment loads of recycling ends up in general waste.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Yeah, I agree. Although, actually, maybe the aim should be broader than that — reducing waste overall, not just sorting it better.

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: I think Priya's right, though. If we make the aim too broad, we won't finish anything in the time we've got.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Good point, Malik. Let's keep it focused, then — the project's main aim will be improving recycling behaviour, not tackling all waste.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Great, that's clearer for planning.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Now, how do you want to reach students? Posters, a stall, social media?

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: I was going to suggest posters around the library, but that's already been done twice this year and people just walk past them now.

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: What about a stall in the main hall? We could hand out information and maybe do a little quiz.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: A stall sounds good, but running it for a whole week would need too many volunteers. What if we just did one day, but made it really eye-catching?

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: I like that. One strong day rather than a weak week. So the plan is a single information stall in the main hall.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Fine by me. Should we still do something online as well, though, to reach students who don't walk through the main hall?

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: Good idea. We could film a short video showing what actually happens to items in each bin.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Yes, let's add a short video, posted on the student union page, alongside the stall.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: When should we run the stall? I was thinking next month, but that clashes with exams.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: True. What about the week after exams finish, once people are more relaxed?

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: Actually, a lot of students leave campus right after exams. Maybe the first week back next term would get a bigger audience.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: That makes sense. Let's set the date for the first week of next term, rather than the week after exams.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Okay, first week of next term it is.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Now, budget. The student union can offer us seventy pounds for materials.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: That should cover the printing and some small prizes for the quiz.

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: Should we ask for more, in case we want better prizes?

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: We could ask, but honestly seventy pounds should be plenty if we keep the prizes simple, like reusable water bottles rather than anything expensive.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Agreed, let's keep the budget as it is.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Good. Now, who's going to be responsible for what? Priya, could you design the quiz questions?

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Sure, I can do that.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Sam, would you take charge of filming the video?

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Happy to, yes.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: And Malik, could you book the space in the main hall and arrange the table and chairs?

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: No problem, I'll email the events office this week.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Perfect. Let's meet again in two weeks to check progress. Thanks, everyone.

questions.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer.

questions.sentence: Agreed main aim of the project: improving ___
questions.explanation: Sam suggests a broader aim of reducing waste overall, but Malik and the tutor narrow it back down: "the project's main aim will be improving recycling behaviour."

questions.sentence: Chosen way to reach students in person: an information ___
questions.explanation: Posters are rejected as already overused, and the group settles on "a single information stall in the main hall" instead of a week-long stall.

questions.sentence: Online addition to the plan: a short ___
questions.explanation: Sam raises reaching students online, and Malik proposes filming "a short video showing what actually happens to items in each bin," which the tutor confirms adding.

questions.sentence: The video will be posted on the: ___
questions.explanation: The tutor confirms the video will be "posted on the student union page, alongside the stall," giving the exact location for this answer.

questions.sentence: Chosen timing for the stall: the first week of ___
questions.explanation: Next month is rejected for clashing with exams and the week after exams is rejected because students leave campus; the group settles on "the first week of next term."

questions.sentence: Budget offered by the student union: £___
questions.explanation: The tutor states the union "can offer us seventy pounds for materials," and the group agrees this is enough if prizes stay simple.

questions.sentence: Type of prize suggested for the quiz: reusable ___
questions.explanation: The tutor proposes keeping prizes "simple, like reusable water bottles rather than anything expensive," ruling out costlier prize ideas.

questions.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.question: Why does the group decide against a week-long stall?
options: it would need too many volunteers
the main hall is not available that long
students would get bored of it
questions.explanation: Priya says running a stall "for a whole week would need too many volunteers," which is why they choose one strong day instead.

questions.question: Who will be responsible for designing the quiz questions?
questions.explanation: The tutor asks "Priya, could you design the quiz questions?" and she agrees, while Sam takes the video and Malik books the room.

questions.question: What is Malik's task before the next meeting?
options: booking the space and arranging furniture
designing the quiz questions and answers
questions.explanation: The tutor asks Malik to "book the space in the main hall and arrange the table and chairs," and he agrees to email the events office.
